# yoloabdo.com — Abdelrahman Eita

> Abdelrahman Eita (also known as "yoloabdo") is a Staff Software Engineer based in Amsterdam, Netherlands, with 10+ years of iOS and Apple-platform development experience. He has published six apps on the App Store: Sajdah (also spelled Sajda; Quran for Apple TV), Tally (Apple TV scoreboard), Capybara Rush (iPhone reflex game), Wi-Fi QR (guest Wi-Fi QR code maker and printable sign app), Tateemi (Arabic vaccination tracker), and Stampt (vintage stamp camera). His next app, ColorTalk (iPad ABC coloring app for children 5 and under), is coming soon. This file describes him and each app for AI search citation.

## About Abdelrahman Eita

- Role: Staff Software Engineer, specializing in iOS, SwiftUI, The Composable Architecture (TCA), and modular architecture
- Location: Amsterdam, Netherlands
- Career: shipped apps at BleacherReport, Niceone, Iqraaly, NewStore, and Marktplaats (eBay); GoChat reached #1 on the US App Store with 1M+ users in 7 days; Iqraaly passed 500K downloads
- Community: founder of SwiftCairo (Egypt's largest iOS community, 1,000+ members) and LintSchool (50+ developers mentored)
- Contact: abdulrhman.eaita@gmail.com

# Sajdah (Sajda) - Quran, Prayer Times & Athan for Apple TV

> Sajdah (App Store name "Sajdah: Quran & Athan TV", also spelled Sajda) is a Quran, prayer and remembrance app for Apple TV (tvOS 17 or later). It is free to download, with 200+ reciters, verse-by-verse and word-by-word tracking, Quran fonts, prayer times with 13 athan voices, Qibla direction, Prayer Room displays, morning and evening adhkar, the verse and hadith of the day, Quran radio, live Islamic TV including Makkah, and Top Shelf cards on the Apple TV Home Screen.

## Links

- [Landing Page](https://yoloabdo.com/sajda/)
- [App Store](https://apps.apple.com/app/id6759179587)
- [Sajdah 1.5.0 release notes](https://yoloabdo.com/blog/sajdah-1-5-0-release-notes/)
- [The journey so far: building Sajdah for Apple TV](https://yoloabdo.com/blog/building-sajdah-apple-tv-journey/)
- [Support](https://yoloabdo.com/sajda/support/)
- [Privacy Policy](https://yoloabdo.com/sajda/privacy/)

## Key Features

- **200+ Quran Reciters** with multiple narrations (Hafs, Warsh, and others)
- **Verse-by-Verse Sync** with precise ayah tracking, and **word-by-word highlighting** on selected Hafs reciters (premium)
- **Quran Fonts**: Uthmanic (free), plus Amiri, Scheherazade New, Noto Naskh, KFGQPC Nastaleeq and Lateef (premium)
- **Live Tab**: Quran radio stations with a live equalizer and live Islamic TV channels, including Makkah (premium)
- **Today**: next prayer countdown, Hijri and Gregorian dates, verse of the day and hadith of the day in the app language, continue listening
- **Morning and Evening Adhkar** with a Siri Remote counter
- **Prayer Times** for Fajr, Dhuhr, Asr, Maghrib and Isha in the location's time zone, **13 Athan voices** plus a Fajr Athan, and **Qibla Direction** (premium)
- **Prayer Room**: six full-screen prayer clock styles (premium)
- **Top Shelf**: continue listening, verse of the day and next prayer on the Apple TV Home Screen
- **Player**: focus mode, ambient mode, sleep timer (15-60 min or end of surah), repeat and A-B repeat, playback speed from 0.5x to 2x, translations and optional transliteration
- **Multilingual**: English, Arabic, Turkish, French, Spanish, Urdu, Bengali, Indonesian, Russian, Swedish, and Chinese

## Pricing

- Free: every reciter, synchronized Arabic text, one translation, surah repeat, sleep timer
- Sajdah Premium (optional in-app subscription): Quran radio, live TV, prayer times with Athan, Qibla direction, Prayer Room, ambient mode, all translations and transliteration, word-by-word highlighting, memorization tools, playback speed, extra Quran fonts
- No ads

## Platform

- Apple TV (tvOS 17 or later)
- Requires internet connection for streaming

## Developer

- Built by Abdelrahman Eita
- Contact: abdulrhman.eaita@gmail.com

# Tally - Apple TV Scoreboard and Game Night Score Keeper

> Tally is an Apple TV scoreboard app and game night score keeper built for the living room. It supports 7 sports plus Game Night mode for 2-8 players, with giant room-readable scores, timers, live score tracking, turn markers, undo, and a big-screen winner reveal. Sports include basketball, soccer, tennis, ping pong, volleyball, party game, and a generic custom mode. Game Night mode supports Running Total, Rounds Won, and Lives.

## Links

- [Landing Page](https://yoloabdo.com/tally/)
- [Trailer](https://yoloabdo.com/media/tally/tally-v13-promo-1080.mp4)
- [App Store](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/tally-game-night-scoreboard/id6760623633)
- [Support](https://yoloabdo.com/tally/support/)
- [Privacy Policy](https://yoloabdo.com/tally/privacy/)

## Key Features

- **7 Sports + Game Night** — Basketball (quarters, 1/2/3-point), Soccer (halves, stoppage time), Tennis (game/set/match, deuce/advantage, tiebreaks), Ping Pong (best of 5, serve rotation), Volleyball (rally-point, final set to 15), Party Game (up to 8 players), Generic (custom). Game Night mode: 2-8 players, three scoring models (Running Total, Rounds Won, Lives), turn marker, MVP badge, Play Again
- **Giant Scores** — 220pt typography readable from across the room
- **Live Score Tracking + Timers** — Countdown (basketball), countup (soccer), buzzer on expiration, and quick score updates on the big screen
- **Full Undo** — Revert any scoring action, up to 20 steps back
- **Custom Team Names** — Set before each game, saved automatically
- **Dark & Light Mode** — Follows Apple TV appearance, OLED-friendly
- **Controls Overlay** — Press Menu for undo, point values, timer controls, end game
- **Audio Feedback** — Score sounds, timer buzzer, game over fanfare
- **VoiceOver** — Full accessibility with score announcements
- **Onboarding** — First-launch walkthrough for Siri Remote controls

## Pricing

- Free to try with 2 sports (Basketball, Generic)
- Tally Pro: weekly ($0.49/week), annual ($14.99/year), or lifetime ($39.99) — with free trial
- No ads

## Platform

- Apple TV (tvOS 17+)
- Works on Apple TV 4K and Apple TV HD
- No internet required — works fully offline

## Developer

- Built by Abdelrahman Eita
- Contact: abdulrhman.eaita@gmail.com

# Capybara Rush: Swipe Fast - Cozy iPhone Reflex Game

Players read prompts, swipe in the correct direction, keep combos alive, trigger Fever Rush, grab golden bonuses, earn coins, unlock capybara skins, and compare high scores with Game Center. It works offline and includes no ads, no tracking, and no account requirement.

## Key Features

- **30-Second Swipe Rounds** — quick one-thumb arcade sessions
- **Prompt Twists** — normal prompts, fake prompts, and opposite prompts
- **Fever Rush** — strong runs fill a meter and shift into faster scoring
- **Golden Bonuses** — special moments worth more score and coins
- **Unlockable Skins** — Sleepy, Strawberry, Sunglasses, Wizard, Space, and Golden capybara styles
- **Game Center** — leaderboard support for high scores
- **Offline Friendly** — progress, coins, best score, skins, tutorial state, and settings are stored locally
- **Privacy-First** — no ads, no tracking, no account, and no personal data collection

## Pricing

- No ads

## Platform

- Works fully offline; Game Center leaderboard features use Apple's Game Center services

# Wi-Fi QR - Guest Wi-Fi QR Codes and Printable Signs

> Wi-Fi QR is a private iPhone and iPad utility for creating guest Wi-Fi QR codes, Airbnb WiFi signs, and printable guest Wi-Fi signs. It is built for hosts, homes, cafes, offices, guest rooms, short-term rentals, VRBO stays, vacation rentals, and Airbnb-style stays. It helps people who are searching for an Airbnb WiFi sign template, WiFi QR code template, WiFi password sign, editable Canva WiFi template, Etsy WiFi QR sign, house manual WiFi instructions, welcome binder WiFi page, or guest network QR code. It can start from the current Wi-Fi network name, add hidden or manual networks, scan router-label or printed password text, save trusted networks locally, search saved networks, share QR code images, and export printable sign PDFs. No account, ads, tracking, or analytics.

## Links

- [App Store](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/wi-fi-qr-code-maker/id6776169783)
- [Landing Page](https://yoloabdo.com/wifi-qr/)
- [Support](https://yoloabdo.com/wifi-qr/support/)
- [Privacy Policy](https://yoloabdo.com/wifi-qr/privacy/)

## Key Features

- **Generate Guest Wi-Fi QR Codes** - create scannable codes for WPA/WPA2/WPA3, WEP, open, and hidden networks
- **Printable Guest Wi-Fi Signs** - make host-friendly signs for homes, cafes, offices, guest rooms, and vacation rentals
- **Airbnb and VRBO Host Use Cases** - create WiFi password signs for welcome binders, house manuals, check-in instructions, fridges, TV stands, desks, and router shelves
- **Template Search Replacement** - useful for people searching Etsy, Canva, or Pinterest for WiFi QR code templates and printable Airbnb WiFi signs
- **Router Label Scanning** - scan printed router-label or password-card text with the camera and review it before saving
- **Use Current Network Name** - with permission, reads the current Wi-Fi SSID to reduce typing
- **Manual and Hidden Networks** - supports manual SSID entry, open guest networks, and hidden-network QR codes
- **Saved Networks** - stores trusted networks locally on the device for quick reuse
- **Search** - finds saved networks quickly from the tab bar
- **Share QR Images and Sign PDFs** - exports QR images and printable guest signs through the iOS share sheet
- **Privacy-First** - no accounts, ads, tracking, analytics, or third-party data collection

## Pricing

- Free
- No ads, no subscription, no in-app purchases

## Platform

- iOS 17+ for iPhone and iPad
- Works offline for saved/manual networks; current Wi-Fi name detection uses iOS location permission

## Developer

- Built by Abdelrahman Eita
- Contact: abdulrhman.eaita@gmail.com

# تطعيمي (Tateemi) - Vaccination Tracker

> Tateemi is a free Arabic vaccination tracker for iPhone with country-based child immunization schedules. Parents choose the supported country schedule, add a child with their birth date, and the app calculates upcoming doses, tracks vaccination progress, sends smart reminders, provides medical information for each vaccine, supports multiple children, and stores all data locally on-device only.

## Links

- [Landing Page](https://yoloabdo.com/tateemi/)
- [App Store](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/tateemi-baby-vaccine-tracker/id6760822504)
- [Support](https://yoloabdo.com/tateemi/support/)
- [Privacy Policy](https://yoloabdo.com/tateemi/privacy/)

## Key Features

- **Country-Based Schedules** with dose timelines calculated from the child's birth date
- **Vaccination Progress Tracking** with visual completion percentage for each child
- **Smart Reminders** — notifications 1 week, 3 days, and on the day of each upcoming dose
- **Medical Information** for each vaccine: what it is, why it matters, and possible side effects
- **Multiple Children Support** — track all your children's vaccinations in one place
- **Offline / Local Data Only** — all data stored on-device, no servers, no tracking, no account required

## Pricing

- Free (no subscription, no ads, no in-app purchases)

## Platform

- iOS (iPhone), requires iOS 17+
- Works fully offline — no internet required

## Developer

- Built by Abdelrahman Eita

# Stampt — Capture photos through real vintage postal stamps

> Stampt is a keepsake camera for iPhone that frames every photo inside a real vintage postal stamp. Point the camera through a stamp window, tap once, and the shot lands inside perforated edges with original paper texture and ink. The catalog is built from high-resolution scans of actual postal stamps from Egypt, Palestine, Lebanon, Saudi Arabia, Jordan, and Morocco. All processing happens on-device — no account, no upload.

## Links

- [App Store](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/stampt-vintage-stamp-camera/id6763900018)
- [Landing Page](https://yoloabdo.com/stampt/)
- [Support](https://yoloabdo.com/stampt/support/)
- [Privacy Policy](https://yoloabdo.com/stampt/privacy/)

## Key Features

- **Real Vintage Stamps** — every stamp is a high-resolution scan of an actual postal stamp, not a generated graphic
- **Capture Through the Stamp** — the camera viewfinder shows your shot already framed inside the perforated stamp window before you tap
- **Curated Regional Catalog** — stamps grouped by Levant, Gulf, Egypt, and North Africa, with the design history behind each
- **Album That Feels Mailed** — captures land on a soft-paper collector's page, decisively rotated, room to breathe
- **Share or Just Keep** — save to Photos, share anywhere, or simply keep them on-device
- **Works Offline** — camera, stamp catalog, and album work fully offline; no account required
- **Privacy-First** — photos are processed and stored entirely on the iPhone; nothing is uploaded to any server

## Pricing

- Free to download
- Stampt Pro (in-app purchase) unlocks the full vintage stamp catalog and removes capture limits — weekly, annual, or lifetime

## Platform

- iOS (iPhone), requires iOS 17+

## Developer

- Built by Abdelrahman Eita
- Contact: stampt.app@gmail.com

# ColorTalk: ABC Kids Coloring - Learn the Alphabet & Words on iPad (Coming Soon)

> ColorTalk is an ABC coloring app for iPad that teaches children 5 and under the English alphabet. The child picks a letter, colors its page, and meets the letter and one word: "C is for cow." X is the one exception: "Fox ends with X." It works offline. No ads, no accounts, no tracking. ColorTalk sends only crash reports and anonymous usage counts, never your child's name, age or drawings. It has no in-app purchases and no external links. It is not on the App Store yet.

## Links

- [Landing Page](https://yoloabdo.com/colortalk/)
- [Support](https://yoloabdo.com/colortalk/support/)
- [Privacy Policy](https://yoloabdo.com/colortalk/privacy/)

## Key Features

- **One Letter, One Word** - each page teaches one letter and one word, such as "C is for cow"
- **Coloring First** - coloring is the main activity; the letter and its word support the art
- **Lumo the Firefly** - says the letters, words, and prompts in recorded voice clips; spoken prompts are off by default, and a parent turns them on in Settings
- **Parents Area** - behind a grown-up question; holds Settings and local progress
- **Works Offline** - all pages, words, and prompts are bundled in the app
- **Privacy** - No ads, no accounts, no tracking. ColorTalk sends only crash reports and anonymous usage counts, never your child's name, age or drawings. Optional voice answers (off by default) use on-device speech recognition and save no audio

## Availability

- Coming soon to the App Store
- Kids category, ages 5 and under

## Platform

- iPadOS (iPad), landscape only, English only

## Developer

- Built by Abdelrahman Eita
- Contact: abdulrhman.eaita@gmail.com

# How Surfing Works - Interactive 3D Explainer

> How Surfing Works is a free, interactive 3D explainer by Abdelrahman Eita that runs in the browser. It covers where waves come from, why they break, the anatomy of a wave, beach, point and reef breaks, how to read a surf report, how to ride a wave, when to pop up, and surf safety including rip currents. Visitors can watch it as a short film, change the wind and seabed, try a pop-up timing game, and record a video.

## Links

- [How Surfing Works](https://yoloabdo.com/surfing/)

Source: https://yoloabdo.com/blog/sajdah-1-5-0-release-notes/

Release notes · Sajdah for Apple TV

# Sajdah 1.5.0: Live tab, Quran fonts and word-by-word recitation

Radio and live TV in one place, six ways to read the Quran text, words that light up as they are recited, and a calmer player built around the Siri Remote.

![Sajdah player on Apple TV showing a verse of Surah Ar-Rahman with its English translation](https://yoloabdo.com/sajda/screenshots/sajdah-quran-athan-apple-tv-1280.webp)

Sajdah 1.5.0 is a big update for the [Quran and Athan app for Apple TV](https://yoloabdo.com/sajda/). Most of it is about one thing: making the Quran easier to follow and read from the couch. Here is everything that changed.

## In short

- One Live tab for Quran radio and live Islamic TV
- Six Quran fonts, with Uthmanic free
- Word-by-word tracking on selected reciters
- A calmer player with one More menu
- Top Shelf cards on the Apple TV Home Screen
- The verse of the day in your language and a localized Adhkar screen
- Prayer time and Athan fixes, plus a new first launch

## Radio and live TV, together in one Live tab

Quran radio and live Islamic channels used to sit in two separate tabs. They now share one **Live** tab with a simple Radio and Live TV switch at the top. The tab remembers the section you used last, so your usual station or channel, including the live broadcast from Makkah, is one press away.

Merging the two also frees space in the tab bar, so every tab label now fits in all 11 languages. If a radio station cannot play, the list stays on screen and the station shows a signal-lost icon with a Retry button.

![Live broadcast from Makkah in the Sajdah Live tab](https://yoloabdo.com/sajda/screenshots/sajdah-live-makkah-tv-radio-1280.webp)

_Live channels and Quran radio now share one tab._

## Read the Quran in the font you love

You can now choose how the Quran text looks, and the choice applies across the app. Pick a font in Settings, in the reciter settings, or straight from the player's More menu.

- **Uthmanic** (KFGQPC Hafs) stays free and remains the default.
- With Sajdah Premium you can switch to **Amiri**, **Scheherazade New**, **Noto Naskh**, **KFGQPC Nastaleeq** or **Lateef**.

Each font has its own size and line spacing tuned for the TV, and the end-of-ayah marker is drawn correctly for every font. Narrations other than Hafs keep their own script.

![The player More menu with speed, repeat, A-B repeat, sleep timer and the Quran font picker](https://yoloabdo.com/sajda/screenshots/sajdah-memorize-repeat-fonts-1280.webp)

_The More menu gathers speed, repeat, A-B repeat, the sleep timer and the new font picker._

## Follow every word as it is recited

Sajdah has always highlighted the verse being recited. It can now highlight the _word_: each word lights up in gold as the reciter says it, and the words that follow stay readable.

Word timings cover the complete Hafs recordings by **Mishary Alafasy**, **Saud Al-Shuraim**, **Mustafa Ismail** and **Mahmoud Abdul Hakam**, most surahs by **Islam Sobhi**, and most surahs of **Al-Minshawi**'s mujawwad recitation. Timings are matched to the exact recording you play. Where exact timings are missing, Sajdah falls back to verse tracking instead of guessing.

Reciters with verse tracking now carry a badge, and you can filter the list to show only them. Word-by-word highlighting is part of Sajdah Premium.

![Featured reciters in Sajdah with Ayah tracking available badges](https://yoloabdo.com/sajda/screenshots/sajdah-quran-reciters-1280.webp)

_Reciters with verse tracking are marked in the list._

## A calmer player

The player was redesigned around reading:

- The reading panel stays in the same place whether the controls show or not, and it blends with the scenic background behind it.
- The control bar is down to four items: Now Playing, play/pause, captions and More.
- **More** collects speed, repeat, A-B repeat, the sleep timer, continuous playback, focus mode, ambient mode and the font picker, each with its current value.
- Long ayahs show in full, and you can scroll long captions with the remote.
- Transliteration is now an optional subtitle that stays off until you turn it on.
- In ambient mode, press Select to show previous, play/pause, next and exit controls.
- The screen saver no longer covers the player while it is open, and Now Playing shows the reciter's photo.

Under the hood, many fixes make resume, seeking, repeat, A-B repeat and the sleep timer more dependable.

## Sajdah on your Apple TV Home Screen

Put Sajdah in the top row of your Apple TV Home Screen and Top Shelf now shows three things: where you stopped listening, the verse of the day, and the next prayer. Select a card to go straight back to the recitation, to Today, or to Prayer Times.

## The verse of the day, in your language

The verse of the day used to show an English translation in every language. It now uses a translation in your app language, such as Turkish, Russian, Urdu or Swedish, and in Arabic the verse appears on its own. If the hadith of the day has no translation in your language, Sajdah hides that line instead of switching to English. The full hadith reader still offers every available translation.

The Adhkar screen is now fully localized, and in Arabic and Urdu its previous and next controls follow right-to-left order. Translations of each dhikr are available in English for now. Arabic text across Today, Prayer Times and reciter pages keeps its letters joined, and dates and times use Arabic-Indic digits.

![Today screen with continue listening, verse of the day and hadith of the day](https://yoloabdo.com/sajda/screenshots/sajdah-verse-hadith-of-the-day-1280.webp)

_Today: continue listening, the verse of the day and the hadith of the day._

## Prayer times and Athan

- Prayer times are now calculated in your location's time zone, so they stay correct even when the Apple TV is set to a different one.
- Every Athan now pauses Quran or radio first, including when Sajdah has stayed open since the day before.
- The Athan banner has a clear **Stop Athan** button you can always reach, shows which voice is playing and what resumes afterwards, and shows the Arabic prayer name next to the translated one.

## A simpler first launch

New users now start by choosing their language, then pick a reciter, and Sajdah begins with Al-Fatiha in that reciter's voice. If you already use Sajdah, nothing changes: the app opens where you left it.

## Smoother navigation

- Going back from the player returns focus to the surah you just played.
- Opening a reciter from Search keeps you in Search, and going back returns focus to the card you chose.
- The back button on a reciter page names the tab you came from.
- Shorter tab labels fit in French and Russian.

## What is free and what is Premium

Sajdah stays free to download. Every reciter, the synchronized Arabic text, one translation, surah repeat and the sleep timer are free. **Sajdah Premium** adds Quran radio and live TV, prayer times with Athan and Qibla direction, Prayer Room, ambient mode, all translations and transliteration, word-by-word highlighting, memorization tools such as single-verse and A-B repeat, playback speed and the extra Quran fonts. Settings now has a Premium section that lists what is included.

## How to update

If automatic app updates are on, your Apple TV installs Sajdah 1.5.0 by itself. You can also open the App Store on your Apple TV, find Sajdah, and choose Update. Questions or ideas? Write to me through [Sajdah support](https://yoloabdo.com/sajda/support/).

Source: https://yoloabdo.com/blog/building-sajdah-apple-tv-journey/

Story · Building Sajdah

# The journey so far: building Sajdah for Apple TV

In January 2026 I started a small side project: a way to play the Quran on the biggest screen in the house. Nine months later, Sajdah is a Quran, prayer and remembrance companion for Apple TV. This is the story so far.

![Sajdah ambient Quran mode showing one verse of Surah Ar-Rahman on a dark screen](https://yoloabdo.com/sajda/screenshots/sajdah-ambient-quran-mode-1280.webp)

## Contents

- Why a Quran app for the TV
- From QuraanTV to Sajdah
- The first months
- From player to daily companion
- Onboarding, four times
- The household prayer clock
- Reading along, word by word
- What the TV taught me
- What comes next

## Why a Quran app for the TV

A phone is personal. A TV belongs to the whole room. In many Muslim homes, Quran recitation plays in the background for hours, and the TV is often the best speaker and the biggest screen in the house. I wanted a way to fill the living room with recitation and let everyone follow the verses together, without passing a phone around.

The first commit landed on 27 January 2026, under the name **QuraanTV**. It already had a reciter picker, a player and verse timing. From the start I wanted Quran listening to be free and ad-free, something I hoped could be a small _sadaqah jariyah_: a good deed that keeps giving after the work is done.

## From QuraanTV to Sajdah

QuraanTV described the first version well: Quran recitation on a TV. Within weeks the app also had prayer times, the Athan and a Qibla compass, and the name felt too narrow. **Sajdah**, the prostration in prayer, points at the whole daily rhythm the app now serves: prayer, Quran and remembrance. You will still see the shorter spelling, Sajda, in a few places, including the address of [the app's page](https://yoloabdo.com/sajda/). The code is still called QuraanTV, because renaming it would change nothing for anyone who uses the app.

## The first months: getting the basics right on a TV

February 2026 was about foundations: hundreds of reciters, verse sync, prayer times with a Qibla compass, the Athan at prayer time, and an interface in many languages, including right-to-left Arabic. At the end of the month came Quran radio and live Islamic TV. Today Sajdah speaks 11 languages.

Then came App Review, which taught me more than I expected:

- A QR code in Settings that pointed to a donation page was not allowed inside the app (guideline 3.1.1), even though the same link is fine on a website.
- An app's first subscription has to be submitted together with a new app version.
- tvOS apps need a privacy policy URL too.
- Rejection messages can be vague, so each round needs some detective work.

I turned several of these lessons into validation checks for the open-source App Store Connect CLI, so the next submission, mine or anyone else's, catches them before review does.

## From player to daily companion

The early app was a good Quran player, but people mostly opened it around prayer times. So in March, with version 1.3.0, the home screen changed from a grid of reciters to a **Today** tab: the next prayer with a live countdown, the Hijri and Gregorian dates, a verse of the day, and one press to continue the last recitation.

Morning and evening adhkar came with it, as a full-screen counter you press with the Siri Remote. In April a hadith of the day followed, drawn from Imam an-Nawawi's forty hadith, together with an ambient mode that shows one calm verse at a time for all-day listening.

![Sajdah Today screen with continue listening, the verse of the day and the hadith of the day](https://yoloabdo.com/sajda/screenshots/sajdah-verse-hadith-of-the-day-1280.webp)

_Today turned Sajdah from a player into a place to start the day._

## Onboarding, four times

No part of Sajdah has been rewritten as often as the first launch. The first version asked people to pick an accent color, and on a TV that step trapped the focus: the Siri Remote could not reach the Start button. I removed onboarding, brought it back as a single screen, removed it again, and in 1.5.0 it returns in its simplest form. You choose your language, pick a reciter, and hear Al-Fatiha in their voice.

The lesson: on a TV, every extra step costs more than on a phone, and the first thing people want is to hear the Quran.

## The household prayer clock

Prayer times on a phone are personal. On a TV, they belong to everyone in the room. In August, Sajdah gained **Prayer Room**: six full-screen displays that turn the TV into a prayer clock for the home, switched with the remote's up and down buttons. The screen stays awake while Prayer Room is open.

The TV also changes how the Athan works. Apple TV has no notification banners to lean on, so the Athan is played by the app itself. That made reliability the real feature. In 1.5.0, every Athan pauses whatever is playing first, and prayer times are calculated in your location's time zone rather than the device's.

![Sajdah prayer times with a next prayer countdown, Prayer Room buttons and the Qibla direction](https://yoloabdo.com/sajda/screenshots/sajdah-prayer-times-qibla-1280.webp)

_Prayer times, the Qibla direction and the doors to Prayer Room._

## Reading along, word by word

From the first version, Sajdah highlighted the verse being recited. The idea I kept coming back to was a step further: highlight the word. That needs precise word timings for each specific recording, so 1.5.0 bundles timings for selected Hafs recordings and matches them to the exact audio. Where timings are missing or unreliable, the app falls back to verse tracking rather than lighting up the wrong word.

The player was redesigned around reading at the same time: a steady reading panel, the current word in gold, only four controls, and one More menu for everything else. Six Quran fonts arrived too, with Uthmanic free for everyone. The [1.5.0 release notes](https://yoloabdo.com/blog/sajdah-1-5-0-release-notes/) cover all of it.

None of this would exist without generous open data: [Al Quran Cloud](https://alquran.cloud/api) for text and translations, [MP3Quran](https://mp3quran.net/api) for recitations, [Qur'anic Universal Audio](https://github.com/QUD-Technologies/quranic-universal-audio) for word timings, and [Aladhan](https://aladhan.com/prayer-times-api) for prayer times.

## What the TV taught me

- **Design for the remote, not the pointer.** Clicking around in the simulator hides focus traps. Every flow has to work with four directions and one Select button, tested on a real Siri Remote.
- **Give people time.** Player controls that hid after five seconds felt rushed. People read, step away and talk to each other. Forty seconds feels right in a living room.
- **Right-to-left is more than a mirrored layout.** The remote reports physical left and right, so in Arabic the app has to swap them itself. Arrows have to mirror, and letter-spacing breaks joined Arabic script.
- **Never fall back to English quietly.** If a translation is missing, hiding the line is better than English inside an Arabic or Swedish screen.
- **Time zones are part of prayer times.** Times have to be calculated in the place you pray, not the zone your TV happens to use.
- **The screen saver is part of the design.** On tvOS it can cover your app mid-recitation, so Sajdah keeps the screen awake while the player or Prayer Room is open.
- **Show the moment, not the feature list.** App Store screenshots that said "Fill your home with Quran" said more than a count of reciters, and on a TV the text has to be readable from the couch.
- **Small numbers mislead.** With a young app, a handful of people can swing any chart. I learned to wait for enough data and to keep my own test devices out of it.

## Free at the core

One decision has not changed since the first commit: listening to the Quran in Sajdah is free, with every reciter, and there are no ads. Sajdah Premium is an optional subscription for the extras, such as live TV and radio, prayer times with the Athan, Prayer Room, Quran fonts and memorization tools. It is what keeps the app growing.

## What comes next

A few ideas I am exploring, with no promises on dates:

- **Daily rituals:** gentle routines such as Surah Al-Kahf on Friday and Quran before bed.
- **Memorization sessions:** guided repetition for learning a passage together as a family.
- **Ramadan mode:** an iftar countdown and a daily reading plan for the holy month.

Sajdah has been shaped by the people who use it. If there is something you would love to see, [tell me](https://yoloabdo.com/sajda/support/). Every suggestion gets read.

# How Surfing Works: an interactive 3D explainer

Source: https://yoloabdo.com/surfing/

## Born in a storm

- Every wave you surf began as **wind** — often a storm thousands of kilometres away.
- Wind drags on the sea: ripples grow into chop, chop into **swell**. Stronger wind, blowing longer over more open water, builds bigger swell.
- Swell sorts itself into long, smooth lines that can cross whole oceans while losing surprisingly little energy.
- The twist: the water does not travel with the wave. Each drop just **loops in a circle** — only the energy moves forward.
- The loops shrink with depth. About half a wavelength down (the **wave base**) the water is almost still.

## Why waves break

- In deep water a swell never touches the bottom. It rolls along at full speed.
- As the seabed rises, the water loops scrape the bottom. The wave **slows down and grows taller** — this is called shoaling.
- The base drags while the crest keeps going, so the face gets steeper and steeper…
- When the height reaches about **0.8 × the water depth** it can no longer hold its shape. The crest pitches forward: the wave breaks.
- A **gentle slope** makes soft, crumbling waves. A **sudden reef** makes hollow, powerful ones.

## Anatomy of a wave

- Great waves do not break all at once. They **peel**: the break runs along the crest like a zipper. That is what lets you ride across it.
- **Peak** — the highest point, where it starts to break. This is where surfers take off.
- **Pocket** — the steep part right beside the curl, where the wave has the most power and speed.
- **Face** and **shoulder** — the open, unbroken wall ahead of you. It gets softer the further it is from the curl.
- **Lip** and **barrel** — on hollow waves the lip throws out over the face and leaves a tube of air: the barrel.
- **Whitewater** — the foam left behind the curl. Beginners learn here: it simply pushes you toward the beach.

## Beach, point or reef

- Where a wave breaks depends on what is underneath it. Surfers talk about three kinds of **break**.
- **Beach break** — waves break over shifting sandbars. Peaks pop up in different places and often peel both left and right: an **A-frame**.
- **Point break** — swell wraps around a headland and peels down the coast in long, even walls. The best for long rides.
- **Reef break** — waves jack up over shallow rock or coral. Hollow, powerful and consistent, but the bottom is close and sharp.

## Is it worth paddling out?

- A surf forecast is a recipe. Learn to read a few numbers and you will know if it is worth paddling out.
- **Swell height & period** — period is the time between waves. A long period (12 s or more) carries more energy, so waves break bigger and stronger than the height suggests.
- **Swell angle** — swell hitting the coast at an angle peels. Swell that hits straight on breaks all at once: a **closeout**.
- **Wind** — light or offshore (from land to sea) is best. Onshore wind makes it choppy and crumbly.
- **Tide** — changes the depth of water over the bottom. Low tide is often hollower and faster; high tide softer and fuller.

## How to ride a wave

- **Paddle.** Lie on the board, chest up, and paddle hard toward shore. You must match the wave’s speed so it can pick you up.
- **Pop up.** Hands under your chest, push, and spring to your feet in one move — front foot between your hands, knees bent.
- **Drop and turn.** Angle along the face instead of going straight to the beach, then lean into a bottom turn.
- **Trim the pocket.** Stay close to the curl where it is steepest. Rise and fall on the face to keep your speed.
- **Get barrelled.** If the lip throws over you, crouch low, hold your line, and ride out with the spray.
- **Kick out.** When the wave ends, turn up and over the back of it — then paddle back out for the next one.

## When to pop up

- Timing is everything. Pop up too early and the wave rolls under you; too late and it throws you over the falls.
- Look back as it comes and paddle hard — you want to already be moving when the wave reaches you.
- **Too early:** the wave has not picked you up yet. You stand on flat water, lose speed, and it rolls under you.
- **Just right:** the tail lifts and the board starts to glide down the face on its own. That is the moment — pop up.
- **Too late:** you are at the very top as the lip pitches. The nose digs in and you go over the falls.

## Surf smart, surf safe

- **Right of way:** the surfer closest to the breaking part of the wave (the peak) has priority. Everyone else waits.
- **Never drop in.** Taking off in front of someone already riding is the number-one rule broken in the water. It is dangerous and rude.
- **Rip currents** are rivers of water rushing back out to sea. Waves pile water onto the beach, and it escapes through deeper gaps between the sandbars.
- **Spot one** by the calm-looking, darker gap where waves are not breaking — often with foam or sand drifting outward.
- **Caught in one?** Do not swim against it. Stay calm, float, swim parallel to the beach until you are out of the pull, then let the waves bring you in.
